title: Matrix Game
body_html:
Matrix Game

A finite zero-sum game is represented by a matrix $A=(A_{ij})_{i \in I,j \in J}$. The maximizing player chooses a row $i \in I$, the minimizing player chooses a column $j \in J$, and $A_{ij}$ is the payoff of the maximizing player. Conversely, any real matrix determines a finite zero-sum game in this way.

References

  • [MFoGT, Chapter 2, Section 2.2, after Def. 2.2.1] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Finite zero-sum games are represented by real matrices.
